solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slipping on hard fish

indicators.note: placed on means put after, so the slipping word follows the hard letter

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
slipping up or going wrong is erring

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing on a fish lying on a hard floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order is reversed: the H for 'hard' comes first in the answer, then the word for 'Slipping'.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a common silvery food fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: At work, Kath itches to retire

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Kath's itching at work makes her want to quit her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' looks like leaving work but here means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit the sack is an informal idiom for going to bed, and retire also means to go to bed.

clue.text: Again hear about score at Twickenham?

parts.note: RE means concerning or about, as in a letter heading
Twickenham is England's rugby stadium, and a try is a score in rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby fan asks to hear again about a score at the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the London home of English rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A court retries a case when it hears it a second time.

clue.text: Lying, perhaps, in wrong church with religious class

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
CE is the Church of England
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Someone is lying in the wrong church while attending a religion lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying is one way of being insincere: saying what one does not truly mean.

clue.text: Instrument leaders of group used in the auditorium rarely

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: The heads of a band seldom play a certain instrument in the concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The guitar is a stringed musical instrument, plucked or strummed.

clue.text: I've messed up zero operations

parts.note: the digit zero looks like the letter O
OPS is a short form of operations, as in military ops

explanation.surface: A surgeon confesses to a blunder: no operations got done.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone blurts out on noticing a small blunder of their own.

clue.text: Old female repeatedly absent

parts.note: repeatedly says the female letter comes again, a second F

explanation.surface: An old woman keeps missing from her usual place.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is off work today is away from it, not present.

clue.text: Sign left on hospital department

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A notice has been left on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the two pieces in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen or warning sign of something to come.

clue.text: Junk that is ignored by husband

indicators.note: the husband is left out, so his letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: taken as the word THAT, the 'is' joining it to what follows

explanation.surface: A wife complains about rubbish that her husband takes no notice of.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods or rubbish.

clue.text: Fighter plane tilts over before burning

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for tilts is read backwards

parts.note: to tilt something is to tip it
a fire is a burning

explanation.surface: A warplane rolls over before going up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the reversal signal; 'before' simply puts the first piece ahead, and 'burning' is read as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supermarine Spitfire was the famous British single-seat fighter of the Second World War.

clue.text: Stuffing own loot casually under child's bed

indicators.note: in a down answer, the rearranged letters sit below the cot

parts.note: a cot is a baby's bed with sides

indicators.note: done casually, the letters are tossed into a loose new order

explanation.surface: Someone casually hides their loot beneath a child's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' is the anagram signal for 'own loot'; 'under' places that below the child's bed in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton wool is soft fluffy cotton used as padding or filling.

clue.text: Somewhat windy ahead, knocking back Austrian composer

indicators.note: knocked back, the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A walker reports a breezy stretch ahead that knocks them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' takes NDYAH from 'windy ahead'; 'knocking back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian composer known as the father of the symphony.

clue.text: Rated new company's architectural style

indicators.note: made new, the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A firm's style of building has been freshly rated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RATED into ARTDE; the 's joins CO to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s, seen in many buildings.

clue.text: Article by magazine about graduate crossing one African country

parts.note: THE is the definite article

indicators.note: turned about, the magazine's word is read backwards
the graduate's letters are crossed by the one, which sits across the middle

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A magazine article about a graduate who crosses an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the magazine; 'crossing' has the one lying inside the graduate's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small West African state along the River Gambia.

clue.text: American Society occupying congress area in SE England

indicators.note: the American and society letters take up a place inside the other word

parts.note: congress in the sense of sexual intercourse
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American society holds its congress in a region of south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'congress' looks like a political assembly but means sexual intercourse. SUSSEX is a county on the English south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex is a historic county on the south coast of England, now split into East and West.

clue.text: Mysterious flash around plug

indicators.note: the flashy word goes around, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: flash as an adjective means showy or ostentatious
a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad

explanation.surface: A camera flash goes off around an electric plug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flash' and 'plug' both look like nouns from photography and electrics; they are SHOWY and AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowy means vague, obscure and hard to make out, like something mysterious.

clue.text: Go away to live with a bird

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to share a home with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a slang command telling someone to leave at once.

clue.text: Nothing disturbs even throwing game

indicators.note: the nothing letter breaks into the other word, disturbing it from inside

parts.note: being quits means being even, with no debt either way
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing upsets a game of throwing, even so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbs' looks like an anagram signal, but it places O inside QUITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits is a game in which rings are thrown to land over a peg.

clue.text: Companion with cake failing to open large country house

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: the cake's word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a gateau is a rich layered cake

explanation.surface: A friend brings a cake that collapses before it can be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to open' drops the G of GATEAU, leaving ATEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or grand manor house in the countryside.

clue.text: Crime Harry scorns regularly

indicators.note: letters are taken at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: A man named Harry looks down on criminal behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and every other letter of 'Harry scorns'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Hindu instructor moved through water against current

parts.note: to have swum is to have moved through water, so swam
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A Hindu teacher swam upstream against the flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' means next to here and just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man.

clue.text: Arm perhaps supporting priest with doctor

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A priest backs a doctor in a cause, perhaps by armed force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the arm as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A human arm is one instance of a front limb of a four-limbed animal.

clue.text: Finish part of bowls match

definitions.meaning: to finish something is to bring it to a close, to conclude it
in lawn bowls a match is played in rounds, each one of bowling towards the jack in one direction

explanation.surface: Finish part of a bowls match.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawn bowls is a British green game where bowls are rolled towards a small ball, the jack.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is both a conclusion and one round of play in bowls or curling.

clue.text: Silver ring gone

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone mourns a silver ring that has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past, as in 'long gone' or 'years ago'.

clue.text: Observed envoy on vacation with newsman

indicators.note: vacated, the word is emptied of its inner letters, leaving its ends

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A diplomat on holiday was spotted with a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To have eyed something is to have looked at or watched it.

clue.text: Dog that is left on bridge

indicators.note: placed on means put after, so these letters follow the bridge word

parts.note: to span is to bridge, and a span is a bridge's arch
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dog has been abandoned on a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The spaniel is a breed of gundog with long drooping ears.
